edit.description: the `src/job.ts` cites move to the files that now decide

summary: with the verbs gone `src/job.ts` is named for nothing it holds — an ignore set, a loose queue read, a friction count and a live-pid read, four jobs and no job
acceptance: `src/job.ts` does not exist; the ignore set is its own module and each other survivor sits in the file its name already is.
notes: Target shape: `RUNTIME_IGNORES`, `mergeIgnoreLines`, `ensureRuntimeIgnores`, `frictionIgnoreEntry` → `src/runtimeIgnores.ts`; `countFrictionFiles` → `src/friction.ts`; `liveLoopClaim`/`liveLoopPid` → `src/pidClaim.ts`; `readPendingLoose` → `src/pendingLedger.ts`. Behavior-free: the typecheck, the suite and the export and citation pins hold it. `spec/jobs.md` keeps its name — `harness/ignores.ts` and `src/cli.ts` still cite *Runtime ignores*.

edit.description: a section walking the job cut; the opening paragraph and the grep block take it

summary: the 0.17 note opens by saying neither break is in the API, which the job cut falsifies — four verbs, two selectors, `Chain.seedDir` and a dispatcher option all go
acceptance: docs/MIGRATING-0.17.md walks each API break the job cut lands with before and after, and its opening paragraph and section-applicability grep name them.
notes: One entry rather than a section per cut entry: the page is a single append-only file, and three entries contending on it is the fanout-width cost the changelog gate was removed for (`spec/cli.md`, *Versioning policy*). The before/after is `flume job run <name>` → a `git worktree add` checkout with its own `.flume`.

edit.description: the rows leaning on the loader fact shrink to a cite
the recorder's doc comment and its posixOnly block shrink to a cite
the case's comment cites the loader section rather than the `.cmd` one

summary: the loader fact has a home now, but five sites still spell it out and two of them cite the `.cmd` section for a shebang subject, so the next fixture restates it a sixth time
acceptance: every site leaning on the win32 loader fact states only what is specific to its own case and cites the section that holds the fact; no shebang-spawn subject cites the `.cmd`-shim section for it.
notes: The rows: `tests/bin.test.ts::bin/flume symlink walk`, the harnessChain command-gate row, the harnessRunner path-separator row, and the two cli.test.ts git-floor rows whose reason names a `.cmd` refusal over a shebang plant. The setup-restore row is the model — case-specific reason, then the cite. No tests[]: a section cite is unresolved by the citation pin (`tests/commentCitations.test.ts`), and prose read against prose is out of scope.

edit.description: the one listing of the channel; the harvest and the count read it
`frictionFiles` takes the engine's listing instead of its own walk

summary: the engine gives its friction channel's listing no home, so the walk is spelled at four sites and the fourth is the package rebuilding a fact the engine holds

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: one exported listing in `src/friction.ts` answers what the declared channel holds; the bare `friction` verb, the count, the teardown harvest and `harness/friction.ts` all read it, and no second walk survives.
notes: Target shape: `frictionNotes(dir)` in src/friction.ts — the sorted direct-child files `isDotName` does not skip. Blocked because `countFrictionFiles` sits in src/job.ts today and src/friction.ts already imports it, so a call the other way closes the job.ts -> chainLoad.ts -> friction.ts cycle; the ignore-set entry moves it into src/friction.ts first.
